opportunities.title: Propose vulnerability identity key and lifecycle schema
opportunities.summary: ### Summary Inspect the committed Anchore JSON fixtures and propose a schema for tracking vulnerabilities over time. Specifically: what combination of fields uniquely identifies "the same vulnerability" across scans? Candidates to evaluate include CVE ID alone, CVE + package name, CVE + package name + version, and CVE + package + image. Write up the tradeoffs, pick a recommendation, and sketch the analytics DB table(s) needed to support first_seen / last_seen / fixed_at / ignored_at / cleared_at fields. **Tech notes:** The Anchore JSON schema is documented at the Anchore project site; worth skimming before diving into fixtures. The goal of this spike is a decision, not code — resist the urge to start implementing. ### Acceptance criteria - [ ] Written proposal (markdown doc in PR) covering identity key options, tradeoffs, and a recommendation - [ ] Proposed analytics DB schema with column types and rationale - [ ] At least one worked example from the fixtures showing how the identity key behaves across days - [ ] Reviewed and approved by Brandon and/or Matt before next ticket starts ## Bounty: $250 This issue has been selected for our paid contributor program. opportunities.summary: `computeStepReward` penalises a step by its token cost, so a step whose adapter reported no usage receives **no cost penalty at all** and scores as more efficient than one that reported honestly. The reward prefers the step it knows least about. ```ts // agents/orchestration/puppeteer-helpers.ts:74 const costPenalty = (output.tokensUsed * 0.00001) / config.maxCost; const timePenalty = output.durationMs / config.maxTime; const efficiencyPenalty = (costPenalty + timePenalty) * config.efficiencyWeight; return progressReward - efficiencyPenalty; ``` Since #4744 an unmeasured step carries `tokensUsed: 0` with `tokensMeasured: false`. opportunities.summary: `source.md` contains the complete RFC 5322 specification (Internet Message Format). We need a **fully conformant email address parser** in Python that implements the complete ABNF grammar from sections 3.2 through 3.4, plus obsolete syntax from §4.4. This parser must handle every edge case defined in the RFC — not just simple `user@domain` patterns, but the full complexity of quoted strings, comments, folding whitespace, group addresses, and domain literals. ## Background RFC 5322 defines email address syntax through a chain of ABNF productions that build on each other: ``` address = mailbox / group mailbox = name-addr / addr-spec name-addr = [display-name] angle-addr angle-addr = [CFWS] "<" addr-spec ">" [CFWS] addr-spec = local-part "@" domain local-part = dot-atom / quoted-string / obs-local-part domain = dot-atom / domain-literal / obs-domain ``` Each of these references further productions (CFWS, FWS, quoted-pair, dtext, etc.) that span multiple sections. **You must read `source.md` completely** to trace the full grammar dependency chain. ## Requirements ### 1. opportunities.title: DashboardShell's active-nav-item highlighting uses exact pathname equality, so nested routes never highlight their parent section
opportunities.summary: `src/components/dashboard/DashboardShell.tsx` determines the active sidebar item with: ```ts const active = pathname === item.href; ``` This is an exact string match. The maintainer/sponsor nav includes items like `{ label: "Bounty pipeline", href: "/issues", icon: GitPullRequest }` and `{ label: "Milestones", href: "/milestones", icon: Milestone }`. When a maintainer navigates from the pipeline board into a specific bounty (`/issues/abc123`, reached via `PipelineBoard.tsx`'s own links), `pathname` becomes `/issues/abc123`, which is not `=== "/issues"` — so "Bounty pipeline" loses its active/highlighted state exactly while the user is drilled into a page that's conceptually still part of that section, with no other sidebar item taking its place. The result is a sidebar that appears to have "nothing selected" whenever the user is on any nested route under a top-level nav destination, which is a common and expected navigation state (viewing one bounty out of the pipeline) that this exact-match check doesn't account for. Suggested fix: use a prefix check for non-root items (`pathname === item.href || pathname.startsWith(item.href + "/")`) so nested routes keep their parent section hig

opportunities.title: parse_duration drops the days (d) unit
opportunities.summary: ## Bug `parse_duration` silently drops the **days** (`d`) unit. The README lists `d` as a supported unit, but the parser ignores it and returns a wrong (too-small) result instead of raising or counting it. ### Reproduction ```python from duration_utils import parse_duration parse_duration("1d") # -> 0 (expected 86400) parse_duration("2d4h") # -> 14400 (expected 187200) ``` ### Expected `d` should be counted as 86400 seconds, so `parse_duration("1d") == 86400` and `parse_duration("2d4h") == 187200`. ### Notes The `d` character is already accepted by the token regex, so malformed-input detection still passes — the value is just never added. A fix should add the `d` unit and cover it with tests. /bounty $50
